raw_response:
I’m in Quzhou and this 5 mu is my main land, so I won’t do anything fancy this year. I’ll keep the wheat-maize rotation on all 5 mu, same as usual, because that is the safest way for me to keep grain coming and avoid too much market risk. I only finished middle school, so I do listen when people talk about fertilizer rates and timing, but in the end I still go by what I saw on my own field. Last year the wheat did better when I put enough base fertilizer and then added some urea at jointing, so I’ll do that again. Water costs money, but if I save too much on irrigation and the crop suffers, that loss is bigger. Since some family members work off-farm, I also need a plan that fits the labor we actually have. So I’ll keep the land in wheat first, then plant maize right after harvest without delaying, use hybrid seed from the local dealer, apply moderate fertilizer instead of the highest rate, and irrigate when the crop stage really matters.

For wheat I use a bit more fertilizer and more water because wheat in our area responds clearly if managed well, especially at jointing.
